subject: Hosted API commit uplift, staged rollout & operational MOP
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@snackcart.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity increase & renewal options

Mateo,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. We wanted to follow up with specifics so we can get procurement moving. Current snapshot: SnackCart is on the hosted API with a 500M token monthly commit, monthly billing. Over the last quarter our peak windows have grown 3x and we're hitting soft-throttle events during mid-day promotions.

Request: we'd like to increase to ~1.5B committed tokens/month, with a staged uplift (so engineering can validate). Key asks from our side:
- A predictable rate-band model (baseline, burst window, and a soft-throttle behavior) so our frontend engineers can handle retry/backoff.
- Clarity on pricing bands for committed vs overage, and any volume discount for annual prepay.
- Billing cadence options (monthly invoice vs annual PO) and invoicing net-60.
- SOC2 evidence for our security team and a short ops runbook for canary rollouts (especially region failover).

I've attached a procurement_summary.xlsx with our projected token curve and preferred billing terms. Can you share a proposed uplift plan and a mutual action plan (MAP) we can use for procurement?

Cheers,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform Engineering, SnackCart
elena@snackcart.com

Attachment: procurement_summary.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@snackcart.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity increase & renewal options

Hi Elena — thanks for the detail and the spreadsheet, that helps a lot. High-level proposal below; attached is a concise proposal PDF for procurement.

Proposal (initial):
- Staged uplift: Month 1 baseline -> 1.2B committed tokens, Month 2 -> 1.35B, Month 3 -> full 1.5B. This gives your engineers a rolling canary window to validate client-side retry/backoff behavior.
- Rate bands & soft-throttle: Baseline QPS band for the new commit, a defined burst window (30% above baseline for 10-minute windows), and soft-throttle behavior with headers to indicate retry-after and degrade to smaller model variant if desired.
- Pricing: we table a volume-discount schedule in the attached PDF (we'll confirm exact numbers once procurement indicates billing cadence). Annual prepay receives preferential unit pricing; monthly invoicing is available at standard commit pricing.
- Billing: we can accept PO with net-60 for ARR contracts; for the staged uplift we typically align invoicing on the month of uplift.
- Compliance/ops: attaching a short MOP and SOC2 evidence checklist. Vivek, can you confirm capacity/region availability (us-east primary w/ us-west failover) and any ops notes?

Next steps:
1) Elena confirms preferred billing cadence (monthly vs annual prepay).
2) SnackCart to share PO or redlines; our legal will review.
3) We will provision the staged uplift and schedule a joint canary run (we recommend a 30-day canary with 7-day monitoring window).

Attachment: redwood-proposal-snackcart-v1.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Pricing and ops notes for SNCK-2027-047

Internal notes (no external recipients):
- Deal id: SNCK-2027-047. Recommend the following price bands to propose in the updated PDF: baseline commit unit price, commit uplift discount of 9-12% at 1.2B+, and a further acceleration discount for annual prepay. Keep negotiation room for 3-4% additional discount tied to multi-year.
- Ops recommendation (Vivek): staged uplift as Mateo proposed + a 30-day canary. Also recommend configuring automatic model-fallback for burst windows (smaller quantized variant) to avoid hard throttles for user-facing flows.
- Risk items: SnackCart asked for net-60. Finance needs a credit review and procurement to sign off on SLA credits. If they require an extended invoicing term, include conditional clause: payment term accepted with a 1.5% net credit reserve until first invoice clears.
- Action: Mateo to propose MAP and capture PO, Vivek to provide runbook and SRE on-call schedule for the canary. Lauren to prepare onboarding checklist for dedicated support.

Karthik
VP Sales Operations

From: SnackCart Contracts <contracts@snackcart.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Redlines to proposal and billing term request

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: Raj Patel <raj@snackcart.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:44:00 -0700
Subject: Redlines to proposal and billing term request
To: contracts@snackcart.com

Mateo / Redwood team,

Thanks — procurement has reviewed the attached proposal and made a small set of redlines:
- Remove automatic renewal. We prefer an explicit renewal at the end of term rather than auto-renew.
- Billing: request net-60 and PO-based invoicing for the first 12 months.
- Limit the soft-throttle fallback to defined endpoints (we will provide a short list of critical endpoints to exclude from fallback).

I've attached the redlined MA Plan (SnackCart_MA_Plan_v2.pdf). Please confirm acceptance or propose alternative language.

Thanks,
Raj Patel
Director, Procurement, SnackCart

Attachment: SnackCart_MA_Plan_v2.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@snackcart.com>, Raj Patel <raj@snackcart.com>, contracts@snackcart.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redlines to proposal and billing term request — next steps & MAP

Hi Elena / Raj — appreciate the redlines and the clarity. Short answers and next steps below.

1) Auto-renew: we can accommodate removing auto-renew for the first 12-month term; we'll add an explicit renewal trigger with 60-day notice instead.
2) Billing: net-60 PO-based invoicing is acceptable for the first 12 months pending credit review (Finance will confirm credit terms this week).
3) Soft-throttle exclusions: fully ok — please send the list of endpoints to exclude and we'll add that as an appendix to the runbook.

Mutual Action Plan (MAP) — key milestones:
- Today (May 20): Redwood accepts redlines above, prepare updated MA Plan and DocuSign envelope.
- May 21–24: SnackCart legal/procurement sign and return PO.
- May 25–28: Provision staged uplift (1.2B), schedule canary kickoff with SnackCart SRE.
- June 25: Target completion of staged rollout to 1.5B assuming canary success; weekly check-ins during canary.

Attachments & links:
- Updated MA Plan (we'll send a final PDF with the redlines incorporated).
- DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/0a1b2c3d-snck-2027-047
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/SNCK-2027-047

I'll send the updated MA Plan and the DocuSign envelope shortly; Lauren will send the onboarding checklist and Vivek will follow up with the runbook.

Thanks everyone — excited to get this moving.

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood-updated-ma-plan-draft.pdf (PDF, 38KB)
